laws.layer: each nonterminal layer projects the current typed guidance obligations, enumerates candidate operations, deterministically selects one through the guidance scheduler, executes exactly that operation, applies typed resolutions into a derived immutable guidance state, and receipts the complete transition
laws.completion: semantic completion is read only from guidance completion law; nonempty lookup rows, one successful hop, one path, one candidate or one executed operation cannot terminate the forward pass
laws.progress: a successful nonterminal layer must produce at least one typed resolution and a distinct next guidance state; silent no-op layers are invalid when progress is required
laws.ordering: candidate operations are canonicalized by operation identity before scheduling so provider enumeration order cannot change the selected operation or layer receipt
laws.authority: the guidance scheduler retains hard authority and terminal-completion validity; the forward-pass provider cannot force an ineligible operation by ordering or execution output
laws.resources: layers, provider calls, projected queries, candidate operations, resolutions, resource cost, IO and database operations are independently bounded and produce typed limiting dispositions
laws.replay: program initial state projections enumeration receipt decision execution receipt resolution set guidance transition and final state are deterministically BLAKE3 receipted
